reason: This text fragment (Exodus 2:16-22) is a narrative account of Moses meeting the daughters of the priest of Midian at a well. It describes shepherds driving away the women, Moses intervening to help them, and subsequently being invited to stay with their family and marry Zipporah. The passage contains no blame directed at any leaders or at Yahweh, nor does it depict the Hebrew people expressing concern about being put at risk. It is simply a narrative episode in Moses's life before his call to lead Israel, with no element of the Hebrew people criticizing their leadership or divine protection.
